clue.text: Wild solution, with a degree of overlap, is something to have on hand

indicators.note: overlap means the two words share a letter where they meet, so one copy of that letter is dropped

blocks.note: a solution to a problem or illness

explanation.surface: A chemist recommends a strong solution to keep handy, apparently with some overlap in its uses.
explanation.walkthrough: The two words share their C where they join, so it is written only once: MANI-CURE.
explanation.definitionFit: A manicure is a cosmetic treatment of the fingernails, literally something you have done on your hand.

clue.text: Be uncertain about atmospheric dampness and what it may cause

blocks.note: mist is fine water droplets in the air

explanation.surface: Doubts about the damp air and the corrosion it might bring.
explanation.definitionFit: To mistrust is to doubt or be suspicious of something, i.e. to feel unsure about it.

clue.text: Most of the booze overturned in the dark

indicators.note: most of a word is all but its final letter
turned over in a down clue means the letters are read from the bottom up

explanation.surface: Most of the drink gets knocked over in the darkness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the' looks like part of 'in the dark', but it is fodder: most of it plus GIN, all reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: Night and dark are used interchangeably, as in 'after dark' meaning after nightfall.

clue.text: Conservative drive for discipline

explanation.surface: A Conservative campaign for stricter discipline.
explanation.definitionFit: To chasten is to discipline or correct someone, especially by punishment.

clue.text: Uphill standard must accommodate motorway slope

indicators.note: going uphill in a down answer means the letters run from the bottom up
to accommodate is to house, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: M as in M1, a British motorway

explanation.surface: A rule about steep roads: a motorway gradient must meet a standard.
explanation.walkthrough: PAR read upwards is RAP, which takes M inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A ramp is an inclined surface joining two levels, a slope.

clue.text: Part of hooter having indecisive sound after a month

explanation.surface: A car horn makes a hesitant noise after a month of use.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' places the hesitation sound behind the month. Hooter is British slang for the nose, not a car horn here.
explanation.definitionFit: The septum is the wall of cartilage dividing the two nostrils, a part of the nose (slang hooter).

clue.text: European historical article to be held up as a bad influence

indicators.note: held up in a down answer means lifted, so the letters read upwards

blocks.note: the old form of 'the', as in 'Ye Olde'
to live is to be, to exist

explanation.surface: A European history piece is held up as a harmful influence.
explanation.walkthrough: E, YE and LIVE are joined and the whole lot is turned upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The evil eye is a supposed curse cast by a look, a malign influence on whoever receives it.

clue.text: That letter, fourth time rejected, rubbished society magazine

indicators.note: time is the abbreviation T, and rejecting the fourth occurrence of it removes one such letter
something rubbished is trashed and messed up, so the remaining letters get jumbled

explanation.surface: A letter to a society magazine is rejected for the fourth time and binned.
explanation.walkthrough: THAT LETTER has four Ts; drop the fourth and rearrange the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tatler is a long-running British magazine covering high society and fashion.

clue.text: Help secured by knights, say, yet to win

indicators.note: secured by means held fast within, so one piece sits inside the other

blocks.note: knights are chess pieces, which are called men

explanation.surface: Help for knights who have not yet won a joust.
explanation.walkthrough: Knights are chess pieces, and chess pieces are collectively called men; 'yet to win' is racing jargon.
explanation.definitionFit: A maiden in horse racing is a horse that has never won a race.

clue.text: Writer with an oddball description of peaceful times?

indicators.note: an oddball is eccentric and out of the ordinary, so the letters are put in a strange order

explanation.surface: An eccentric writer describes an era of peace.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the definition is loose: the period between wars is peaceful only by comparison.
explanation.definitionFit: Interwar describes the years between two wars, especially 1918–39, a period without major conflict.

clue.text: Very important article about married railway worker

blocks.note: signal as an adjective means notable, outstanding

explanation.surface: An important newspaper piece about a married man who works on the railways.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Signal' as an adjective, as in a signal achievement, means very important; 'about' here only places the article beside married, an unusually loose use.
explanation.definitionFit: A signalman operates the signals and points from a signal box, a classic railway job.

clue.text: Warrior tribe held back in reserve at first

indicators.note: something held back is pulled the other way, so the little word before it is read right to left
at first puts the word it follows at the front of the answer

blocks.note: ice is a cool, distant manner, i.e. reserve
taken as written, then turned round

explanation.surface: A warlike tribe keeps its reserves back at the start of battle.
explanation.walkthrough: The Iceni were the ancient British tribe led by Boudicca.
explanation.definitionFit: The Iceni were an Iron Age people of East Anglia who rose against Rome, a tribe famed for war.

clue.text: What 14 will do: decay at end of use

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, so only that is kept

explanation.surface: A note on how a spinning wheel ages: it decays once it is out of use.
explanation.definitionFit: 14 is the spinning wheel, and turning round on its axle is exactly what a wheel does.

clue.text: Evening music found in Sweden before enthralling another Scandinavian on the rebound

indicators.note: rebounding means bouncing back, so the Scandinavian is read backwards
to enthral is to hold captive, so one word holds the other inside it

explanation.surface: A Swede falls for a rebounding Dane and courts them with music at night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Evening music' is literal: the word comes from Italian sereno, the open evening sky.
explanation.definitionFit: A serenade is music sung or played at night, traditionally under a lover's window.

clue.text: Son fixing weak part of foot? This offers something to help with knitting

definitions.text: This offers something to help with knitting

blocks.note: fixing in place, as with a pin

explanation.surface: A son straps up a weak heel, then turns to knitting.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark ends the wordplay; the definition is a cryptic description.
explanation.definitionFit: A spinning wheel twists fibre into yarn, supplying the wool that is then knitted.

clue.text: Writerly folk failing to start vote to discard books again and again

definitions.note: adverbial phrase defining an adjective; read as 'happening again and again'

indicators.note: failing to start means the first letter never appears
discarding throws something out, here the abbreviation for a set of scriptures

blocks.note: the Old Testament, the books removed

explanation.surface: Literary types keep failing to start voting, discarding books repeatedly.
explanation.walkthrough: LITERATI loses L; VOTE loses OT, leaving VE.
explanation.definitionFit: Iterative describes a process that repeats, done over and over in cycles.

clue.text: Like an emperor, note, one Iran scrapped

indicators.note: something scrapped is broken up, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An imperial style, noted after one Iranian regime was scrapped.
explanation.definitionFit: Neronian means in the manner of Nero, the Roman emperor famed for tyranny and excess.

clue.text: Left after meal to pen book still topping the lists?

indicators.note: to pen is to enclose, as in a sheep pen, so one piece goes inside

blocks.note: food left after a meal is uneaten

explanation.surface: Leftovers after a meal are used to write a book that stays a bestseller.
explanation.walkthrough: B goes inside UNEATEN after the first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A team that is unbeaten has not lost, so is likely still top of the league table.

clue.text: Lighthouse overseers, three working in British navy, standing beside tree

indicators.note: something working is in operation, its parts moving, so these letters are rearranged
in puts the reworked number inside the navy abbreviation
standing beside puts the tree next to the rest

blocks.note: the elder is a shrub or small tree

explanation.surface: Three lighthouse inspectors serve in the British navy, posed beside a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: Trinity House is the body that runs lighthouses in England and Wales; its senior members bear this title.
explanation.definitionFit: The Elder Brethren are the governing members of Trinity House, the body responsible for lighthouses in England and Wales.

clue.text: Remove top from bowl made of wood

explanation.surface: Take the lid off a wooden bowl.
explanation.definitionFit: To dishelm is an archaic verb for removing someone's helmet, the protective covering on the head.

clue.text: Evict number of people

blocks.note: second meaning: the attendance at an event

explanation.walkthrough: The phrasal verb 'turn out' and the noun for attendance share their letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn out someone is to evict them; a turnout is the count of those who attend, as at an election.

clue.text: Papers about type of speech not entirely found in Cyprus?

indicators.note: not entirely means a word is cut short by its final letter
about means going round, so the papers wrap the shortened word

explanation.surface: Documents on a partial dialect found in Cyprus.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks Cyprus as an example of the answer rather than a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Cyprus is an island in the eastern Mediterranean, so an island is what you find there.

clue.text: Last performance — effectively as Desmond, N?

blocks.note: surface reading: a character called Desmond, perhaps on stage
setter's reading: the film star who played Norma Desmond in Sunset Boulevard, written surname first with initial, as in a cast list

explanation.surface: A final performance, given in the role of someone listed as Desmond, N.
explanation.walkthrough: Gloria Swanson played Norma Desmond in Sunset Boulevard. 'Desmond, N' is a name in surname-initial form, so the actress appears the same way: surname then her initial G.
explanation.definitionFit: A swan song is someone's final performance, from the legend that swans sing just before dying.

clue.text: Grand Dickensian character showing resentment

blocks.note: G is short for grand, a thousand
Barnaby Rudge, title character of a Dickens novel

explanation.surface: A grand Dickens character displays bitterness.
explanation.definitionFit: A grudge is a lasting feeling of resentment against someone.

clue.text: Head start in rebuilding planet destroyer

indicators.note: rebuilding puts the parts together in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Getting a head start on rebuilding a superweapon.
explanation.walkthrough: In Return of the Jedi the Empire is rebuilding the second Death Star, so the surface fits the film.
explanation.definitionFit: The Death Star is the Star Wars battle station that destroys the planet Alderaan.

clue.text: See 24
I start to loosen in time, becoming nimble

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter, so only that is kept
in places the preceding pair inside the word for time

blocks.note: an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: Someone loosening up over time finds themselves getting nimbler.
explanation.walkthrough: I and L go inside AGE.
explanation.definitionFit: Agile and nimble are synonyms: quick and light in movement.

clue.text: A powerful car tails off? My trip needs something much more powerful

definitions.text: My trip needs something much more powerful

indicators.note: with their tails off, the two words lose their final letters

explanation.surface: A boast that a powerful car runs out, but a much bigger trip needs more power.
explanation.walkthrough: Both STRONG and AUTO lose their last letter. The definition is spoken by the answer: a space traveller's trip needs a rocket, far more powerful than any car.
explanation.definitionFit: An astronaut travels into space, a journey that needs a rocket, far more powerful than any car.

clue.text: Imagines quantities of Scotch without English

indicators.note: without in its old sense means outside, so one piece wraps round the other

blocks.note: a dram is a measure of whisky

explanation.surface: Someone fantasises about plenty of Scotch whisky without any English involvement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking', but here it means outside: DRAMS goes round E.
explanation.definitionFit: To dream is to imagine or fantasise, so dreams matches imagines as a third-person verb.

clue.text: Irritation I overlooked in environmentally aware German girl

indicators.note: something overlooked is left out, so that letter is removed
in places the shortened irritation inside the green word

explanation.surface: An irritation goes unnoticed in an eco-conscious German girl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Environmentally aware' is the political sense of green, as in the Green Party.
explanation.definitionFit: Gretchen is a German girl's name, a diminutive of Margarete, as in Goethe's Faust.
